full_text_en:
Bank of China Jiangxi Branch v. Nanchang City Housing Administration Bureau — dispute over illegal mortgage registration

(This case was decided at the 1268th meeting of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court.)

Ruling Summary

When an administrative organ, in the performance of administrative registration duties, fails to exercise the necessary duty of care, thereby causing property losses to the administrative counterpart, it shall bear corresponding compensation liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State Compensation Law of the PRC.

Administrative Compensation Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2002) Xing Zhong Zi No. 6

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Nanchang City Housing Administration Bureau of Jiangxi Province. Domicile: No. 86 Huanhu Road, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Bai Bo, Director General of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Wu Yongping, lawyer of Jiangxi Taihua Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Zhidan, lawyer of Jiangxi Hongzheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bank of China Jiangxi Branch (successor to the rights and obligations of the former Trust and Consulting Company of Bank of China Jiangxi Branch). Domicile: No. 1 Zhanqian West Road, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Fang Hongguang, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Du Hongmin, lawyer of Jiangxi Wode Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Wenbin, cadre of Bank of China Jiangxi Branch.

On the ground that the appellant, Nanchang City Housing Administration Bureau of Jiangxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau), illegally handled the mortgage registration of a house, causing loan losses to the appellee, the appellee, Bank of China Jiangxi Branch, filed an administrative compensation lawsuit with the Jiangxi High People's Court on August 28, 1996. The Jiangxi High People's Court rendered Administrative Compensation Judgment (1996) Gan Xing Chu Zi No. 2 on December 22, 1999. Bank of China Jiangxi Branch disagreed and appealed to this Court. This Court rendered Administrative Ruling (2000) Xing Zhong Zi No. 5 on February 1, 2001, remanding the case to the Jiangxi High People's Court for retrial. After retrial, the Jiangxi High People's Court rendered Administrative Compensation Judgment (2001) Gan Xing Chu Zi No. 1 on April 4, 2002. Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau disagreed and appealed to this Court. After accepting the case, this Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Adjudicator Zhao Daguang as presiding judge, and acting adjudicators Ma Yongxin and Gan Wen as members, and held a public hearing, with court clerks Tan Wei and Chen Chunmei recording. The appellant's agents ad litem Wu Yongping and Liu Zhidan, and the appellee's agents ad litem Du Hongmin and Xu Wenbin appeared in court. The case is now concluded.

The Jiangxi High People's Court, based on the evidence submitted by the parties and after courtroom cross-examination, found the following facts: On April 5, 1995, Nanchang Tianlong Industrial Group Company (hereinafter referred to as Tianlong Company) applied to the former Trust and Consulting Company of Bank of China Jiangxi Branch (hereinafter referred to as Trust Company) for a loan of RMB 7,000,000, citing the need for working capital to purchase goods. The Trust Company agreed to grant the loan on the condition that Tianlong Company complete the mortgage procedures for the loan and ensure no risk existed for the loan. On April 14 of the same year, Yan Guilong, legal representative of Tianlong Company, applied to Nanchang City Real Estate Transaction Management Office (hereinafter referred to as Nanchang Real Estate Exchange) for mortgage registration of the company's property located at the second floor of No. 29 Chuanshan Road, Xihu District, Nanchang City, with a floor area of 2,482.15 square meters, and submitted the purchase agreement between Tianlong Company and the Second Development Office of Zhongfang Nanchang Real Estate Development Company and Property Ownership Certificate No. 005518. On the same day, the Trust Company commissioned Nanchang City Real Estate Price Appraisal Office (hereinafter referred to as Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office) to appraise the value of the property to be used as collateral for the loan. On April 17 of the same year, Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office issued an (95) Hong Fang Gu Zi "Appraisal Report," appraising the collateral property at 75% of its market value at RMB 6,515,643. On the same day, the Trust Company and Tianlong Company signed a "Loan Contract" for RMB 7,000,000, with a loan term from April 26, 1995 to September 25, 1995, and a monthly interest rate of 10.98 per mille. Jiangxi Xinma Industry Co., Ltd. stated in the loan contract that it agreed to assume guarantee liability for the principal and interest of RMB 500,000. On April 26 of the same year, Nanchang Real Estate Exchange issued No. 0005005 "Notice of Mortgage Loan," determining that the property owner of the property located at No. 29 Chuanshan Road, Xihu District, Nanchang City, with an area of 2,482.15 square meters, submitted by mortgagor Yan Guilong, was Tianlong Company, with property ownership certificate No. 005518, and the mortgagee was the Trust Company, with a mortgage loan amount of RMB 7,000,000, and a mortgage term of five months from April 26, 1995 to September 25, 1995. In the remarks column it noted: "Banks (credit cooperatives) may handle loan procedures upon receipt of this notice and keep this notice; upon maturity of the mortgage loan, the borrower shall apply for cancellation of mortgage registration procedures with this notice and the certificate of full repayment issued by the bank (credit cooperative)." Accordingly, the Trust Company disbursed a total of RMB 7,000,000 to Tianlong Company in three installments on April 26, April 30, and May 3 of the same year. On June 13 of the same year, Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau, in the name of its subordinate Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office, notified the Trust Company by letter that it had discovered that Yan Guilong had not obtained a property ownership certificate from the Municipal Housing Property Registration Office, and had used a fake property certificate to handle mortgage loan procedures. After learning of this, the Trust Company recovered on the next day the unused loan balance of RMB 885,000 from Tianlong Company. On June 16 of the same year, the Public Security Bureau of Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province, filed a case to investigate Yan Guilong's fraud using a fake property certificate to obtain loans, and recovered a Lincoln sedan from Yan Guilong, which was appraised by the Jiangxi Price Appraisal Office at RMB 150,000; additionally, RMB 960,000 in loan interest differentials was recovered. On May 7, 1996, the Trust Company filed an administrative compensation application with Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau as the organ obligated to pay compensation. Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau did not make a decision on whether to pay compensation within the statutory period. On August 28 of the same year, the Trust Company filed an administrative compensation lawsuit with the court.

During the trial of this case, on February 10, 1998, the Trust Company was approved by the Jiangxi Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce to cancel its enterprise legal person registration, and its claims and debts were assumed by Bank of China Jiangxi Branch. Accordingly, the plaintiff in this case was changed from the Trust Company to Bank of China Jiangxi Branch. Tianlong Company, having failed to participate in the 1997 annual inspection, had its business license revoked by Nanchang City Administration for Industry and Commerce in August 1998, and no establishing or supervising unit was found. On October 29, 1999, Yan Guilong was arrested and brought to justice. On October 20, 2000, the Nanchang Intermediate People's Court rendered Criminal Judgment (2000) Hong Xing Yi Chu Zi No. 89, finding that Yan Guilong had used a fake property certificate as collateral to fraudulently obtain a bank loan of RMB 6,500,000, and that after the incident, the public security organs recovered a total of RMB 1,995,000 for Bank of China Jiangxi Branch, causing an actual loss of RMB 4,505,000. His conduct constituted the crime of fraud, and he was sentenced to life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. The judgment became legally effective on November 5, 2000.

The Jiangxi High People's Court held in its trial that Article 4, Paragraph 2, and Article 10 of the "Interim Measures for the Administration of Urban Housing Property Rights and Registration" of the Ministry of Construction, Article 1 of the "Notice on Strengthening the Management of Real Estate Mortgage and Appraisal Related to Bank Loans" (Jian Fang [1995] No. 152) jointly issued by the Ministry of Construction and the People's Bank of China, and Article 3 of the "Notice on Strengthening the Administration of the Real Estate Transaction Market" ([88] Jian Fang Zi No. 17) jointly issued by the Ministry of Construction, the State Price Bureau, and the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, all clearly provide that the real estate administrative authority at or above the county level is the competent department responsible for the administration of urban housing property rights and registration within its administrative region, and handling mortgage registration is a statutory duty of the real estate administrative authority in performing the administrative management of housing property rights and registration. Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau is the administrative authority responsible for handling real estate mortgage registration within the scope of Nanchang City. As its subordinate unit, Nanchang Real Estate Exchange exercised the administrative authority of real estate mortgage registration and should be regarded as acting on behalf of the Bureau, and the Bureau should bear the corresponding administrative legal liability. During the performance of the administrative authority of handling housing mortgage loan registration, the staff of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau failed to carefully examine whether the property ownership certificate of the non-residential house on the second floor of No. 29 Chuanshan Road, Xihu District, Nanchang City, submitted by Yan Guilong as the loan collateral, matched the contents of the ledgers and archives of the same property ownership certificate, and also failed to carefully verify the authenticity of the certificate and seal, thereby erroneously determining that Tianlong Company had ownership of the house, and issued the "Notice of Mortgage Loan," confirming that the housing mortgage legal relationship between the Trust Company and Tianlong Company was valid. This specific administrative act had erroneous factual findings, and its illegality was confirmed by the letter of June 13, 1995, from Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office, a subordinate of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau, to the Trust Company. The Trust Company filed a compensation application with Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau on May 7, 1996, to no avail, and subsequently filed an administrative compensation lawsuit with the court on August 28 of the same year, which complies with the provisions of Articles 13 and 33, Paragraph 1 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC regarding compensation procedures and the statute of limitations for claiming state compensation. The Nanchang Intermediate People's Court has rendered a final judgment in the case of Yan Guilong's fraud of RMB 6,500,000 from the Trust Company, confirming that the loan loss suffered by the Trust Company as a result was RMB 4,505,000. Although the direct infringer of the Trust Company's loan property rights was Yan Guilong, according to the relevant provisions of the Guarantee Law of the PRC and the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC, handling real estate mortgage registration is a prerequisite for the mortgage contract to take effect. The illegal act of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau in handling mortgage loan registration was the main reason why the Trust Company believed there was no risk in granting the loan. Therefore, there is a legal causal relationship between the illegal mortgage registration act of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau and the property loss of the Trust Company. Given that Yan Guilong is unable to repay the loan, Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau shall bear supplementary compensation liability in accordance with the law for the part of the plaintiff's mortgage rights that cannot be realized due to the illegal mortgage registration. According to the relevant provisions of the "Trust Loan Measures of Bank of China Trust and Consulting Company" and the "Approval and Management Rules for Trust Loans of Bank of China Trust and Consulting Company," "The Trust Company shall select enterprises with good reputation and high profits to grant enterprise trust loans." At the time of applying for the loan, Tianlong Company was already insolvent, but the Trust Company, in its approval, erroneously regarded it as an enterprise that "had purchased the ownership of the first to third floors of No. 29 Chuanshan Road for RMB 15,000,000 and owned nearly RMB 21,000,000 in fixed assets," which clearly failed to follow the procedures of project investigation and project evaluation to carefully examine Tianlong Company's creditworthiness and performance ability. There was negligence in the pre-loan review. When granting the loan, it violated the provision that "trust loans shall generally not exceed 60% of the market value of the collateral," and granted a mortgage loan of RMB 6,500,000 at 75% of the collateral's market value. After the loan was disbursed, it failed to carry out any supervision and management as required, resulting in the loan not being used as agreed but rather being used by Yan Guilong within a short period to repay debts and pay other expenses. The plaintiff had obvious fault in causing the loan loss and shall accordingly have the compensation liability of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau reduced in accordance with the law. The plaintiff's claim for interest loss is a potential benefit and does not fall within the scope of direct property losses as defined by the State Compensation Law of the PRC, and therefore is not supported. Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau's arguments that this case does not fall within the scope of state compensation and that the plaintiff's lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations are not legally valid and are not accepted. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 4, Item (4), Article 7, Paragraph 4, and Article 28, Item (7) of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, and Article 29 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases," the judgment is as follows: 1. Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau shall compensate Bank of China Jiangxi Branch for 60% of its loan loss of RMB 4,505,000, i.e., RMB 2,703,000. 2. The remaining claims of Bank of China Jiangxi Branch are dismissed.

Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau disagreed with the judgment and appealed to this Court, arguing: The Trust Company had transferred RMB 2,800,000 to Tianlong Company's account one day before receiving the "Notice of Mortgage Loan" from Nanchang Real Estate Exchange; the loss of this amount had no legal causal relationship with the "Notice of Mortgage Loan" issued by Nanchang Real Estate Exchange, and the appellant should not bear liability for this part of the loss. After the Trust Company had learned that Tianlong Company had used a fake property certificate to handle mortgage registration, Yan Guilong, legal representative of Tianlong Company, still withdrew RMB 360,000 from the Trust Company. The loss of this amount should be borne by the Trust Company itself. When granting the loan, the Trust Company failed to carefully examine Tianlong Company's creditworthiness and performance ability, violated the provision that "trust loans shall generally not exceed 60% of the market value of the collateral," and after the loan was disbursed, failed to supervise the use of funds by Tianlong Company as required. Due to numerous faults in the loan process of the Trust Company, in accordance with Article 5, Paragraph 2 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, if the damage result is caused by the act of the citizen, legal person or other organization itself, the appellant should not bear compensation liability.

The appellee, Bank of China Jiangxi Branch, argued: This case, after multiple rounds of evidence presentation and cross-examination in the original first instance, second instance, and retrial, sufficiently proves that the first instance found that the Trust Company disbursed RMB 7,000,000 to Tianlong Company on April 26, April 30, and May 3. The appellant's claim that the Trust Company had transferred RMB 2,800,000 to Tianlong Company on April 25 lacks evidence. The "Loan Measures of Bank of China Trust Company" and the "Approval and Management Rules for Trust Loans of Bank of China Trust and Consulting Company" are internal management rules of the appellee and do not fall within the scope of laws and regulations. The appellee had no fault in the loan process. Since the loan between the Trust Company and Tianlong Company was a mortgage loan, not a general credit loan, as long as the collateral was risk-free, the loan was also risk-free. As a financial institution, the appellee's loan principal has a capital cost, and interest is statutory fruits, inseparable from the principal, and should be included in the scope of direct loss. The first instance judgment's view that "interest" is a potential benefit and not direct property loss is erroneous.

After courtroom cross-examination, the Jiangxi High People's Court found the following valid evidence provided by the plaintiff: License No. Yin Jin Guan Zi Di 08-0347 issued by the People's Bank of China approving the Trust Company to engage in financial business; the enterprise legal person business license issued to the Trust Company by the Jiangxi Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce; the report of Tianlong Company applying for a loan; the application and approval form for RMB current fund loans of the Trust Company; Yan Guilong's application to Nanchang Real Estate Exchange for handling property mortgage registration and the Trust Company's letter of appointment to Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office for appraising the collateral property; the "Loan Contract" for RMB 7,000,000 signed between the Trust Company and Tianlong Company; the (95) Hong Fang Gu Zi "Appraisal Report" issued by Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office; the No. 0005005 "Notice of Mortgage Loan" issued by Nanchang Real Estate Exchange; the three loan disbursement vouchers for the Trust Company's investment loan payment of RMB 7,000,000 to Tianlong Company; the letter from Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office informing the Trust Company that Tianlong Company had used a fake property certificate for mortgage loan; the investment loan repayment notices issued by the Trust Company showing that Tianlong Company repaid the loan in three installments of RMB 885,000, RMB 150,000, and RMB 810,000, totaling RMB 1,845,000; the copy of the enterprise legal person business license No. 15832068-7-1 issued to Tianlong Company by Nanchang Administration for Industry and Commerce; the Civil Judgment (1995) Hong Min Chu Zi No. 48 rendered by Nanchang Intermediate People's Court. On June 14, 1995, the receipt issued by the Second Department of Nanchang Public Security Bureau for receiving the fake property ownership certificate of Tianlong Company sent by Nanchang Real Estate Exchange; the certificate issued by Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau confirming that the No. 005518 property ownership certificate submitted by Yan Guilong was forged; the Trust Company's application to Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau for compensation and the proof of receipt of the application by Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau; the certificate from Nanchang Public Security Bureau regarding the case filing and investigation of Yan Guilong's criminal fraud and the recovery of stolen assets; the "Appraisal and Appraisal Conclusion on Seized, Recovered, and Confiscated Items" No. Gan Shi Gu Zi [98] No. 03 of the Jiangxi Price Appraisal Office; the "Notice of Approval for Cancellation of Enterprise Legal Person Registration" issued by the Jiangxi Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce regarding the cancellation of the Trust Company's enterprise legal person registration and the assumption of its claims and debts by Bank of China Jiangxi Branch.

The valid evidence provided by the defendant was found to be: The agreement between Tianlong Company and the Second Development Office of Zhongfang Group Nanchang Real Estate Development Company for the purchase of the non-residential first to second floor shopping mall and third floor office building at No. 29 Chuanshan Road, Xihu District, Nanchang City; the copy of the No. 005518 property ownership certificate submitted by Yan Guilong to Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau for mortgage registration; the letter from Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office informing the Trust Company that Tianlong Company had used a fake property certificate for mortgage loan; the materials submitted by Nanchang Real Estate Exchange to Nanchang Public Security Bureau for case reporting; the "Notice on Authorizing the Personnel Establishment of Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau" Nan Bian [1984] No. 47 and "Reply on Approving the Establishment of the Municipal Real Estate Price Appraisal Office and Its Personnel Establishment" Hong Bian Fa [1989] No. 164 issued by the Nanchang Municipal Organization Establishment Committee; the "Registration Certificate for Public Institution Legal Person" Shi Fa Deng Zi Gan 0100182A issued by the Office of the Nanchang Municipal Organization Establishment Committee.

The evidence collected by the court of first instance includes: Materials on Tianlong Company's enterprise legal person registration, incorporation, and revocation of business license from Nanchang Administration for Industry and Commerce; the criminal detention warrant No. (99) 252 for Yan Guilong issued by Nanchang Public Security Bureau; the certificate from Nanchang Housing Administration Bureau to Nanchang Public Security Bureau stating that the numbers and steel seals of property ownership certificates No. 00519 and No. 005518 were forged, with the seal of "Nanchang City Housing Property Administration Bureau" and "Nanchang City Housing Real Estate Administration Bureau" being fake; the records of interviews conducted by Nanchang Public Security Bureau with Trust Company employees Gu Hongwu, Sheng Li, and Liu Jianguang, manager of the Trust Office of Bank of China Nanchang Sub-branch; the "List of the Use of RMB 7,000,000 Loan from the Former Provincial Trust Company to Nanchang Tianlong Industrial Group Company" issued by the Separation Management Department of Bank of China Jiangxi Branch; the Criminal Judgment (2000) Hong Xing Yi Chu Zi No. 89 and the Execution Notice of Nanchang Intermediate People's Court.

The above evidence has been transferred to this Court along with the case file and, upon review, can serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

After courtroom cross-examination, this Court examined the following disputed facts in this case:

Regarding the issue of whether the trust company had already disbursed a loan of RMB 2.8 million to Tianlong Company before the mortgage loan notification was issued. The appellant claimed that the main evidence for this fact was a payment slip submitted by the trust company to the first-instance court, with a stamped date of April 25, 1995, i.e., one day before the mortgage notification was issued. The appellee argued in response that the date stamp was incorrect due to the staff's failure to timely replace the stamp date, and that the written date should prevail, supporting this with other payment vouchers and accounting entries. Upon review, the stamped date on the payment slip submitted by the trust company was April 25, 1995, while the date written by the staff was April 26, 1995. There was an inconsistency between the stamped date and the written date on the payment slip. However, the payment vouchers and accounting entries submitted by the trust company showed both the written and stamped dates as April 26, 1995, and the internal approval documents of the trust company were also dated April 26, 1995. During the first-instance trial, the appellant did not object to the aforementioned evidence submitted by the trust company and expressed no objection to the first-instance court's confirmation that the first loan disbursement date was April 26, 1995. The appellant, during the second-instance proceedings, denied the facts already acknowledged in the first-instance trial but failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove otherwise. Therefore, the appellant's claim that the loan was disbursed one day before the mortgage notification was issued lacked sufficient evidence.

Regarding the issue that after Nanchang City Housing Authority informed the trust company that Tianlong Company had used a fake property certificate to register a mortgage, Tianlong Company still withdrew a loan of RMB 360,000 from the trust company. On June 13, 1995, the Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office, a subordinate unit of the Nanchang City Housing Authority, sent a letter to the trust company stating that Tianlong Company had fraudulently obtained mortgage registration using a fake property certificate. The appellant claimed to have verbally informed the trust company before this date but failed to provide supporting evidence. The appellant further argued that after the letter of June 13, 1995, informing the trust company of the fraudulent mortgage registration, Tianlong Company still withdrew RMB 360,000 from the trust company. This was mainly based on the Prosecution Opinion (Honggongjingsu [2000] No. 2) issued by the Nanchang Public Security Bureau and the Indictment (Hongjianxingsu (2000) No. 079) issued by the Nanchang People's Procuratorate, both provided by the appellant during the second-instance proceedings. However, these legal documents only proved that on June 15 and 19, 1995, Yan Guilong, the manager of Tianlong Company, withdrew RMB 360,000 paid to Jiangxi Great Wall Real Estate Development Company through another person's account. Therefore, the appellant's argument that the trust company failed to take measures to prevent the expansion of losses after learning of the mortgage issue lacked evidentiary support.

Opinion of the Court: In accordance with Article 4, Paragraph 2, and Article 10 of the Ministry of Construction's Interim Measures for the Management of Urban Housing Property Rights and Title Registration; Article 1 of the Notice of the Ministry of Construction and the People's Bank of China on Strengthening the Management of Real Estate Mortgage and Appraisal Related to Bank Loans; and Article 3 of the Notice of the Ministry of Construction, the State Price Bureau, and the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Strengthening the Management of Real Estate Transaction Markets, the Nanchang City Housing Authority is the administrative authority responsible for processing real estate mortgage registration within the jurisdiction of Nanchang City. The Nanchang Real Estate Exchange and the Nanchang Real Estate Appraisal Office, as its subordinate units, carried out administrative acts related to real estate mortgage registration, which shall be deemed as acts performed on behalf of the Authority.

According to the relevant provisions of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC and the Security Law of the PRC, the completion of real estate mortgage registration is a prerequisite for the validity of a mortgage contract. As the administrative authority responsible for handling real estate mortgage registration, the Nanchang City Housing Authority should, in the process of processing mortgage registration, diligently fulfill the necessary duty of care with a high sense of responsibility toward the parties' applications, and should be capable of checking and identifying the authenticity of the mortgaged property and its title certificates. However, in this case, the Nanchang City Housing Authority violated professional standards, failed to fulfill the necessary duty of care, processed mortgage registration for Tianlong Company, which was committing fraud using fake property certificates, and explicitly informed the trust company that it could proceed with the loan. Relying on the trust in the mortgage registration conducted by the property registration authority, the trust company disbursed loans to Tianlong Company, thereby suffering property losses. Although the borrower, Tianlong Company, was the direct cause of the trust company's property losses, the illegal acts of the Nanchang City Housing Authority objectively provided conditions for Tianlong Company to defraud the loan. There is a legal interest and causal relationship between its illegal issuance of the certificate of rights in rem and the trust company's property losses. Pursuant to Article 4(4), Article 7, Paragraph 4, and Article 28(7) of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, and Article 29 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases, the Nanchang City Housing Authority shall bear corresponding liability for negligent compensation for the property losses incurred by the trust company due to its illegal mortgage registration, in the event that Tianlong Company is unable to repay the loan. The first-instance judgment's determination that the Nanchang City Housing Authority should bear supplementary compensation liability was improper and shall be corrected. After the Nanchang City Housing Authority bears administrative compensation liability, it has the right to exercise recourse against Tianlong Company for the amount paid.

During the process of handling the mortgage loan, the trust company failed to carefully review Tianlong Company's credit status and performance capability as required by project investigation and evaluation procedures. The loan amount also did not comply with the prescribed ratio to the market value of the collateral. The trust company bears partial fault liability for the resulting property losses. The trust company's claim that it had no fault in the loan process and should not bear liability cannot be sustained. As a financial institution, the trust company is required to pay interest on deposits held by depositors. The first-instance judgment's determination that interest losses did not constitute direct losses was improper. The trust company's claim that loan interest losses are direct losses and should be compensated should be supported. However, the trust company's request for compensation based on loan interest lacks legal basis. The Nanchang City Housing Authority's arguments that the trust company had already disbursed a loan of RMB 2.8 million to Tianlong Company before the mortgage notification was issued and that the trust company failed to take measures to prevent the expansion of losses after learning of the mortgage issue lack evidentiary support. Its claim that the trust company's fault should entirely exempt it from compensation liability also cannot be sustained. The Jiangxi Branch of the Bank of China may still exercise its claim for actual property losses against Tianlong Company.

In conclusion, upon deliberation by the Judicial Committee of this Court, in accordance with Article 61(3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Item 2 of the Administrative Compensation Judgment (2001) Gan Xing Chu Zi No. 01 of the Jiangxi High People's Court;

2. Amend Item 1 of the Administrative Compensation Judgment (2001) Gan Xing Chu Zi No. 01 of the Jiangxi High People's Court to read: The Nanchang City Housing Authority shall compensate the Jiangxi Branch of the Bank of China in the amount of RMB 2,477,750, plus interest (calculated at the corresponding current deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China from September 26, 1995, to the date of actual payment).

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhao Daguang

Acting Judge: Ma Yongxin

Acting Judge: Gan Wen

September 30, 2003

Clerks: Tan Wei, Chen Chunmei

[Brief Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Zhao Daguang, Senior Judge: Born in 1955, Master of Laws. Served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Administrative Division of the Supreme People's Court since 1998.
